FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `contested_count` fails to exclude findings marked as `exhausted`. The `open_crit_high_count` method explicitly skips exhausted findings (`if e.get("exhausted"): continue`) because they cannot be successfully verified and would block convergence forever. `contested_count` lacks this exact same exclusion. 
FOLLOW: If an exhausted finding retains unresolved challenges, it will permanently inflate the contested count, bypassing convergence checks and forcing the runner to exhaust its maximum rounds or wall-clock limits without making progress.
PROPOSED_FIX:
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
        for e in self.entries.values():
            if e["status"] in _IRRECOVERABLE:
                continue
            # UNCONFIRMED: grace period read-only check
====
        for e in self.entries.values():
            if e["status"] in _IRRECOVERABLE or e.get("exhausted"):
                continue
            # UNCONFIRMED: grace period read-only check
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: C0001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: CONFIRM C0001 | The off-by-one error `round_idx = len(raw_counts) - 1` compares a 0-based index to a 1-based threshold `earliest_stop_round` (e.g. 12). This unconditionally delays the churn-based convergence logic by one full round.
FOLLOW: The system performs an unnecessary extra round of computation, blindly consuming token budget and compute time. Changing it to `len(raw_counts)` correctly aligns it with the 1-based threshold.
PROPOSED_FIX:
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
    round_idx = len(raw_counts) - 1
    churn = rho_avg < cfg.rho_threshold and round_idx >= cfg.rho_earliest_round
====
    round_idx = len(raw_counts)
    churn = rho_avg < cfg.rho_threshold and round_idx >= cfg.rho_earliest_round
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: C0008
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: CONFIRM C0008 | `contested_count` hardcodes `current_round - oldest > 1` instead of using the `grace_period` parameter (which defaults to 2). This defeats dynamic grace period configuration and forces a rigid 2-round delay for unresolved challenges to be counted.
FOLLOW: If a custom grace_period is provided by the orchestrator, the function completely ignores it. Replacing `> 1` with `>= grace_period` mathematically aligns unresolved challenges with the intended, configurable grace window.
PROPOSED_FIX:
<<<< SEARCH bench/reference_runner.py
            if unresolved:
                oldest = min(v["round"] for v in unresolved)
                if current_round - oldest > 1:
                    count += 1
====
            if unresolved:
                oldest = min(v["round"] for v in unresolved)
                if current_round - oldest >= grace_period:
                    count += 1
>>>> REPLACE
VERIFIED: TRUE
